candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the labeled role of IV palonosetron in adults for prevention of both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy.

options.A: Prevention of both acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.
options.B: Treatment of nausea only after vomiting has already begun following chemotherapy.
options.C: Prevention of acute nausea only, with no labeled role in delayed nausea or vomiting.
options.D: Relief of chemotherapy-related pain rather than prevention of nausea and vomiting.

candidate.rationale: Palonosetron is a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist. In adults, its prescribing information includes prevention of both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy. It is administered prophylactically before chemotherapy; it is not an analgesic and its labeled adult indication for moderately emetogenic chemotherapy is not limited to the acute phase.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In adults, palonosetron hydrochloride injection is indicated for prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy and is given as a single IV dose beginning approximately 30 minutes before chemotherapy.
